input.question: How allergy shots work.
input.ground_truth: They inject you with a *really tiny* amount of the allergen at first, then subsequent shots up the dosage a little bit at a time. It exposes your body to the allergen in such a way that it never freaks out and eventually realizes that there isn't actually a threat.

Question: How allergy shots work.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a castle, and the things that make you sneeze or get itchy (like pollen or cat hair) are like little invaders that try to get in.

Now, allergy shots are like sending in a tiny bit of those invaders to the castle *on purpose*, but in a way that’s safe. When your body sees these tiny invaders, it learns, “Hey, these are not really that scary!” So, next time the real invaders come, your body doesn’t get so scared and doesn’t make you sneeze or itch as much.

It’s like showing your body a picture of a cat over and over, so when you see a real cat, you don’t get as scared. That’s how allergy shots help you feel better!
